system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING
PHYSICS CHECK — Governing physical relation is thermal expansion mismatch (ΔL/L = α·ΔT). Current components have mismatched coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE): YSZ electrolyte (~10.5 ppm/°C), Ni-YSZ anode (~12 ppm/°C), LSM cathode (~11 ppm/°C), glass-ceramic seal (~12-14 ppm/°C). Over 775°C ΔT, this generates ~0.8% strain difference, exceeding fracture toughness of brittle glass-ceramic seals after repeated cycling.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components: (1) Replace glass-ceramic seal with compliant mica-based interlayer (commercially available, e.g., Muscovite mica tape) with CTE ~8-10 ppm/°C, (2) Add 50 μm thick porous Ni-foam buffer layer between anode and seal (off-the-shelf, 95% porosity), (3) Apply 2 μm atomic layer deposition (ALD) of alumina on seal surfaces to improve adhesion. Materials: Mica tape, Ni-foam, ALD alumina. Procedure: Cut mica to seal geometry, apply to stack, insert Ni-foam between anode and seal, perform ALD coating in dedicated chamber.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — Standard solution uses rigid glass-ceramic seals with no compliance layers. This approach adds mica and Ni-foam layers, increasing assembly complexity by ~30% and cost by ~15% due to additional materials and ALD process. However, it eliminates seal cracking without adding mass (<1% increase) and maintains manufacturability with standard SOFC stack assembly techniques.
EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Cycle stack between 25°C and 800°C at 5°C/min heating/cooling rates, with 1-hour holds at temperature. Measure open-circuit voltage (OCV) before each cycle and helium leak rate at seal interfaces after every 50 cycles using mass spectrometer. Pass/fail: OCV must remain >1.0V and seal leakage <1% of fuel flow (measured as helium tracer in fuel stream) after 500 cycles. Duration: Test until failure or completion of 500 cycles (approximately 14 days continuous cycling).
